slot.brief: Find the equation of a line through the intersection point of two given lines and satisfying an extra condition (passing through a given point or parallel to a given line).

stem: Find the equation of the line through the intersection of $2x+3y-5=0$ and $4x-3y-4=0$ that also passes through $(0,2)$.

verdicts.working: The intersection is (3/2, 2/3). The line through this point and (0, 2) has slope -8/9, so its equation is 8x + 9y - 18 = 0.

working:
$2x+3y=5,\ 4x-3y=4\Rightarrow (x,y)=\left(\dfrac{3}{2},\dfrac{2}{3}\right);\quad m=\dfrac{\frac{2}{3}-2}{\frac{3}{2}-0}=-\dfrac{8}{9};\quad y-2=-\dfrac{8}{9}x\Rightarrow 8x+9y-18=0.$

Independent check: The intersection is (3/2, 2/3). The line through this point and (0, 2) has slope -8/9, so its equation is 8x + 9y - 18 = 0.
solution:
Solving the two equations gives their intersection $(x,y)=\left(\frac{3}{2},\frac{2}{3}\right)$. The slope of the line through this point and $(0,2)$ is $m=-\frac{8}{9}$, so
$$y-2=-\frac{8}{9}x\quad\Rightarrow\quad 8x+9y-18=0.$$
